title: Merge vs Split: rules for multiword entities (draft log)
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad to collect heuristics for when to merge adjacent tokens into a single entity span vs when to split into multiple labels. This came up while reviewing batch 2025-02 (customers with compound names, product SKUs, and URLs).

Top-level principle (working): prefer semantic atomicity over token adjacency. If two adjacent tokens together form a single semantic object in downstream use (search, analytics, entity linking), prefer merge. If they represent separate attributes or are independently actionable, split.

Concrete rules I'm experimenting with:
1) Proper names with titles/qualifiers: merge when qualifier cannot stand alone for linking. Example: "New York Times" -> merge (ORG). "Dr. Smith" -> merge (PERSON) unless title is explicitly captured as separate label.
2) Product families + modifiers: split when modifier is descriptive and used in filtering. Example: "Galaxy S21 Ultra" -> merge if SKU-level entity needed; otherwise possible split: "Galaxy S21" (product) + "Ultra" (variant) if downstream tracks variants separately.
3) Numeric identifiers + prefixes: merge when prefix is required for uniqueness. "ID 12345" -> merge (IDENTIFIER). But "order 12345" could be split into (ORDER_TYPE=order) + (ORDER_ID=12345) depending on schema.
4) URLs and path fragments: usually split host vs path for analysis; but merge host+port (example: "example.com:8080" -> merge). For query params, treat separately.
5) Hyphenation and punctuation: merge across hyphen when form is lexicalized (e.g., "self-driving" -> merge ADJ). Split when hyphen separates distinct entities (rare).
6) Possessives: generally merge possessive with the noun for person/company ownership: "Apple's Chief" -> merge as PERSON/ORG ownership span, label anchor should be company or person? ambiguous — note to discuss.

Edge cases / notes to revisit: 
- Comma-separated titles: "Amazon, Inc." vs "Amazon Inc" differences in real data; normalization step should remove punctuation before deciding.
- Parenthetical qualifiers: "TensorFlow (v2)" -> prefer merge but capture version as attribute in structured output, not separate entity span.
- Nested entities: "University of California, Berkeley" — one ORG or nested (ORG:University of California + LOC:Berkeley)? Depends on downstream linking; flag as REVIEW if ambiguous.

Annotation examples (quick samples for sanity):
- "San Francisco Bay Area" -> merge as LOC (if geo-region needed), but could be split: "San Francisco" (CITY) + "Bay Area" (REGION) - depends on taxonomy.
- "ACME Corp. product X-12" -> likely split: ORG=ACME Corp. | PRODUCT=product X-12 (but product string should be normalized).
- "john.smith@example.com" -> merge as EMAIL. Do not split at dot.

Heuristic checklist for labelers (quick):
- Ask: will the downstream use treat tokens together? If yes -> merge.
- Is there a stable canonical form that includes both tokens? If yes -> merge.
- Is one token a modifier that will be analyzed separately? If yes -> split.
- If unsure -> mark with "AMBIG" tag and route to review queue.

Operational items / TODOs:
- Draft a short training slide (3 examples per rule) for next labeler sync (target: 2025-10-15).
- Add a small validation script to flag common patterns (emails, IDs, SKU-like tokens) so labelers get suggestions. Linked GH PR idea: GH:repo/labeling-utils#10.
- Create review list of 200 most frequent multiword spans from recent 500k tokens to audit rule coverage (JIRA:DL-412).

Questions for Jonah/Sofia:
- Do we want canonicalization baked into labeling (i.e., label canonical form as metadata) or keep labeling orthogonal and handle mapping later?
- For nested org+loc cases, prefer labeling both spans with nested tags or prefer single top-level span? My lean: allow overlapping labels but flag for linking pipeline.

Quick revision history:
- 2025-02-12 initial notes after batch review
- 2025-04-03 added hyphenation rule after discussion with Jonah
- 2025-06-18 added URL and identifier notes from support ticket DL-376
- 2025-10-06 cleaned examples and action items before sync

Random scratch ideas: capture a short "reason" field in CSV export: "merge: canonical entity" or "split: modifier" — would be super helpful for model training and auditing.

End of scratchpad. Leave as draft until sync outcomes incorporated.
